files.description: Tasting competition scores (96 rows): panel (one of 8 panels, e.g. bread or cheese; 12 entrants each), entrant (person name; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), score (4.0-10.0, one decimal; no empty cells).

task_text: For each panel, give three scores actually given: the score at the position nearest to the lower quartile, the middle score and the score nearest to the upper quartile, where the position of a quartile q is q x (n - 1) counting the sorted scores from 0. Each panel has 12 entries, so two scores are equally near the middle position; then use the lower of the two. `result` should be a table indexed by panel with the columns q1, middle and q3.
intended_computation: Per panel with sorted scores s[0..11]: q1 = s[3] (position 2.75), middle = s[5] (position 5.5, lower neighbour), q3 = s[8] (position 8.25).

predicted_direction.reason: groupby().quantile([...], interpolation='nearest') returned the lower middle score at 0.5 on 2.x, as the task asks; 3.x returns the higher one.

notes: Drafted 2026-11-11 by pkg:TASKS_M2 for catalogue row X02; naive.py shows the invited idiom, reference.py is the version-robust reference.
